aria: Animated recap of the Raptors' 105 to 102 road win over the Pistons: Scottie Barnes' go-ahead driving layup with 14.3 seconds left that made it 103 to 102, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Barnes' 29 points, the top scorers, how the Raptors won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from the Raptors' 105–102 road win over the Detroit Pistons on Nov 20, 2026, from the StatMuse box score, checked against the Associated Press, the Detroit Free Press, MLive, Ball Exclusives and Toronto Raptors On SI. All 105 Toronto points and all 102 Detroit points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (26–28–23–28 to 23–25–24–30) add up to both totals: 54–48 Toronto at the half and 77–72 after three (AP; VAVEL). Team totals (assists 29–20, rebounds 40–33, blocks 4–1, threes made 9–12, free throws made 12–16, 42 of 77 shooting) are from the box score. Toronto's biggest lead of 14 is from the AP, Ball Exclusives and ClutchPoints; Detroit's biggest lead isn't given in any source we could read, so the reel shows only Toronto's. One SI story gives Barnes 27 points; the box score and the other stories have 29. The AP and Ball Exclusives credit Immanuel Quickley with 11 assists; the box score has 10, which adds up to the team's 29. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Toronto ended a six-game losing streak and is 2–1 in NBA Cup group play (AP; Toronto Raptors On SI). Rookie Allen Graves, in his first career start, had 20 points and 10 rebounds for his first career double-double; Quickley's 18 points and 10 assists were his first double-double of the season (Toronto Raptors On SI). Detroit took its first lead of the second half at 93–91 late in the fourth (Free Press). Poeltl's tip-in made it 101–99 with 27.1 seconds left and Cade Cunningham's step-back three put Detroit up 102–101 with 19.8 left (AP). After Barnes' layup, Toronto forced a turnover, Quickley made two free throws for 105–102, Cunningham missed two free throws with 2.2 seconds left and Kevin Huerter's three at the buzzer missed (AP; Free Press; MLive). The Raptors host Milwaukee on Monday, Nov 23 at 7:30 PM ET; they won the first meeting 121–107 at Milwaukee on Nov. 6 (Covers' schedule; AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Scottie Barnes' driving layup with 14.3 seconds left, assisted by Immanuel Quickley, that put Toronto ahead 103–102 for good (play-by-play via Ball Exclusives: "Scottie Barnes makes driving layup (Immanuel Quickley assists)"; Detroit Free Press: "a bullyball drive to the rim with 14.3 seconds on the clock"; MLive: he drove past Cunningham). The board's clock starts at 19.8, the time of Cunningham's three. It is drawn as a finish at the rim after a drive; no source says which side of the floor he attacked. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Toronto Raptors or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Scottie Barnes' listed 6-foot-8 and 237 pounds with No. 4 (Basketball-Reference; RealGM), with his arms scaled to a 7-foot-2¾ wingspan measured at the 2021 draft combine (Bleacher Report). He is drawn in Toronto's road colors with the default figure look (no approved look yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
